groups.title: Parts of a page
groups.text: htmx asks for a part, PAD answers just that part: a {fragment} of the same template, picked by the element htmx swaps. One template for the whole page and for every piece of it.

groups.title: Changing data
groups.text: Posts, edits and carts - the server keeps the state and answers the HTML that shows it, CSRF token and validation included.

groups.title: From the server
groups.text: Parts that come by themselves: after the page, as you scroll, or pushed by the server as events.

examples.title: Active search
examples.lede: The results update as you type. htmx asks the page again with hx-target="#results"; PAD answers the {fragment 'results'} of the same template - the element's name is enough.

examples.title: Lazy loading
examples.lede: The page arrives at once; the slow part - a chart PAD draws - is asked for when the page has loaded, and a skeleton stands in until it comes.

examples.title: Infinite scroll
examples.lede: The last row asks for the next page when it scrolls into view and replaces itself with it - a fragment of rows that ends with the next asker.

examples.title: Inline editing
examples.lede: A row turns into a form and back. Each answer is one row of the same loop - the PHP narrows the rows to the one asked for, padValidate checks the post, the session keeps the edits.

examples.title: Forms without reloads
examples.lede: A {form} with rules= posts through htmx and comes back as its own fragment - refilled with PAD's messages, or as a thank-you. The same rules are checked in the browser first.

examples.title: Out-of-band updates
examples.lede: One answer, two places: the button that was pressed gets its new state, and the cart badge in the header updates too, swapped by its id with hx-swap-oob.

examples.title: Server-sent events
examples.lede: The server pushes HTML: padSse sends a rendered row every second, and htmx's sse extension swaps each one into the page as it arrives.
